root_cause: LoginWorker.login() rejected only null (not empty) username, password and token, and when the userLogin service then failed with requirePasswordChange=Y it returned 'requirePasswordChange' instead of 'error', which LoginWorker.checkLogin() treated as a successful login because it only tested for 'error'.
notes: Fix spans two commits, both on the release18.12 branch: d8b097f (2023-12-14) replaces null checks with UtilValidate.isEmpty() in checkLogin and login; 1dcfa07 (2023-12-15, OFBIZ-12873) makes login return 'error' instead of 'requirePasswordChange' when the userLogin service fails. First fixed release is 18.12.11, but the GitHub mirror has no release18.12.06 to release18.12.11 tags, so refs are commits. The later code execution step uses a separate endpoint and is not part of this root cause.

root_cause: The setup-token setting was not cleared after setup finished and, being a :public setting, was exposed through /api/session/properties, so the setup-only POST /api/setup/validate endpoint stayed callable and tested a database connection built from a caller-supplied H2 JDBC connection string whose driver options can run code.
notes: No public fix commit: the GitHub compare v0.46.6...v0.46.6.1 shows no security commit, and the vendor post-mortem gives no commits. At v0.46.6, src/metabase/setup.clj defines setup-token with :visibility :public and no clearing function, and src/metabase/api/setup.clj defines POST /validate, which checks the token and calls api.database/test-database-connection. Give the audit src/metabase/setup.clj and the H2 driver namespace as well. The Assetnote (now slcyber.io) analysis reports that commit 0526d88f997d0f26304cdbb6313996df463ad13f (January 2022) removed the token clearing; that hash was not checked. Related H2 connection-string bypasses were fixed later as CVE-2023-37470 (0.46.6.4 removed H2 for new connections).

root_cause: Insufficient input validation in UI macros let externally supplied input reach Jelly template evaluation, so it was evaluated as template code on the server.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. The vendor bulletin names the Vancouver and Washington DC Now Platform releases; ServiceNow patched hosted instances and shipped the update to self-hosted customers. No public patch, file or function names.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: DefaultServlet.executePartialPut() named its temporary file after the user-supplied request path with '/' replaced by '.', so with writes and partial PUT enabled a request could create or fill a file whose name equals another resource, including an entry in the default file-based session store that is later deserialized as a session; the fix uses File.createTempFile() and deletes the file after the request.
notes: Fix commit is the one named on the Tomcat 11 security page (fixed in 11.0.3, affected 11.0.0-M1 to 11.0.2); the 10.1.35 and 9.0.99 backport commits were not checked. The bug needs a combination: writes enabled for the default servlet (off by default), partial PUT (on by default), and for code execution also file-based session persistence with the default location plus a deserialization-capable library. Include the session store code (org.apache.catalina.session) in the audit if the tester wants the full combination.

root_cause: The SAML component did not properly validate user input before using it as a fetch destination, so an unauthenticated request could make the server send requests to a chosen location and reach restricted internal resources.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Rapid7's analysis traces the bug to the bundled Shibboleth xmltooling 3.0.2 used by the saml-server process (CVE-2023-36661, fixed in xmltooling 3.2.4): a URI in an XML signature's KeyInfo RetrievalMethod was fetched while processing the signature. That open-source library is a possible stand-in, but it is a different sample.

root_cause: In the pages router, the doRender callback in Server.renderToResponseWithComponentsImpl() fell back to revalidate: 1 whenever a render result carried no revalidate value, so a crafted request that reached this fallback for a non-dynamic SSR route got an s-maxage cache header that upstream caches honored; the fix removes the fallback and sets revalidate = 0 in renderToHTMLImpl().
notes: Fix is 'Remove invalid fallback revalidate value (#69990)': 7ed7f12 is on the 14-2-1 branch (v14.2.10) and bd164d5 on the next-13 branch (v13.5.7). Affected 13.5.1 to 13.5.6 and 14.0.0 to 14.2.9; pages router with non-dynamic SSR routes only. Also give render.tsx to the audit.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: HttpParameters get, contains, remove and appendAll matched parameter names case-sensitively, so during file upload a second parameter whose name differed only in case could replace the already-sanitized upload file name parameter and carry a traversal path into the stored file name.
notes: Both fix commits are titled 'Makes HttpParameters case-insensitive': d8c6969 is on release/struts-6-3-x (fixed in 6.3.0.2) and 162e29f on release/struts-2-5-x (fixed in 2.5.33). The overwritten parameter is consumed by the file upload interceptor (FileUploadInterceptor); include it in the audit together with the dispatcher package.

root_cause: superset/config.py shipped a public constant as the default SECRET_KEY used to sign Flask session cookies, and check_secret_key() at startup only logged a warning when it was unchanged, so a deployment that kept the default accepted session cookies forged with the known key; the fix refuses to start with the default key outside debug or testing.
notes: Fix is PR #23186 ('refuse to start with default secret on non debug envs'), merged on master on 2023-03-01 and first released in 2.1.0; affected up to and including 2.0.1. An earlier commit 412189fc (PR #17984, January 2022) only changed the default value and added the warning. Also give superset/config.py to the audit. The vulnerable condition is a deployment that keeps the default key.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: In the uploads route, the file name identifier arrived URL-decoded (an encoded '/' became a path separator) and ObjectStorage::Concern#retrieve_from_store! used it to build the file path without a traversal check; the 16.0.1 fix adds Gitlab::Utils.check_path_traversal!(identifier) there.
notes: Only GitLab 16.0.0 is affected. The fix commit was not identified; refs are release tags. The retrieve_from_store! code was read at both tags (v16.0.1-ee adds the check_path_traversal! call). uploads_actions.rb is listed as changed by the watchtowr analysis but was not read; give it to the audit together with app/uploaders.

root_cause: When RewriteRule or ProxyPassMatch spliced a loosely matched part of the request target into the proxied URL through variable substitution, mod_rewrite and the proxy canon handlers forwarded the result without rejecting control characters or spaces, so CR and LF in the substituted data split the request sent to the next hop; the fix rejects such query strings with 403.
notes: The httpd security page names r1908095; its git-svn-id shows it is a trunk commit (git d78a166, 'don't forward invalid query strings'). The 2.4.x backport commit was not identified; release tags are 2.4.55 (affected, from 2.4.0) and 2.4.56 (fixed). Only configurations with mod_proxy plus a RewriteRule or ProxyPassMatch that re-inserts captured request-target data are affected. Also give modules/mappers/mod_rewrite.c to the audit.

root_cause: Http1ChunkedEncodingMessageBody.ParseExtension() skipped chunk extensions by scanning ahead to the next CR and only then checking for LF, so a lone LF or CR inside the extension was consumed as extension text and Kestrel saw different chunk boundaries than a front-end that treats a lone LF as a line end; the fix rejects any chunk line ending that is not exactly CRLF with a 400.
notes: PR #64037 ('Fix chunked request parsing') merged into main on 2025-10-15, one day after the advisory; fixed_ref is its merge commit. Serviced releases are 8.0.21, 9.0.10 and 10.0.0-rc2; the servicing branch commits were not checked. The fix also adds an InsecureChunkedParsing AppContext switch that restores the old behavior.

root_cause: On each redirect Client.do() copied headers from the original request through makeHeadersCopier(), but decided whether to strip Authorization, Www-Authenticate, Cookie and Cookie2 only by comparing the previous hop's host with the next one, so headers stripped on a cross-host hop were copied back on a later same-host hop; the fix keeps a stripSensitiveHeaders flag across the whole chain.
notes: CL 643100 (the one the Go vulnerability database lists) is on release-branch.go1.24. Fixed in go1.22.11, go1.23.5 and go1.24.0-rc.2; the backports to the other release branches were not checked.

root_cause: Rows.Scan held the closemu lock only for the RawBytes case, so on context cancellation the background goroutine could close driver.Rows and the connection could be reused by another query while Scan (through convertAssignRows) was still reading driver-owned memory, returning that query's data; the fix holds the close lock for the whole Scan.
notes: CL 693735 is on master. Fixed in go1.23.12 and go1.24.6; the release-branch backports were not checked. Needs parallel queries plus context cancellation during Scan.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: When an entry's size was given both in the ustar header and in a PAX extended header, content was read with the PAX size but poll_next_raw() advanced to the next header using the ustar size, so file content could be parsed as further archive headers; the fix applies the PAX size override before computing the next header position.
notes: Fixed in astral-tokio-tar 0.5.6 (affected up to 0.5.5). The unmaintained upstream tokio-tar (up to 0.3.1) has the same bug and no fix. The advisory also lists RUSTSEC-2025-0111; which RUSTSEC ID maps to which crate was not checked.

root_cause: On Windows, IOCP completion packets already queued for a named pipe could be dequeued after the pipe was deregistered, and mio delivered them with the old token without checking that the pipe was still registered, breaking its promise not to return tokens after deregistration (a use-after-free for tokio, which stores pointers in tokens); the fix keeps the pipe's internal state alive while a completion is in flight and checks registration before returning events.
notes: Windows only. Affected 0.7.2 to 0.8.10, fixed in 0.8.11. 90d4fe0 is the 0.8.x backport named in the advisory; the master fix is PR #1760 (merge commit 6fd5dd0d615a66a30a449d3f8eb1266dad96af62). The fix adds a new event_done completion handler.

root_cause: In simple query mode SimpleParameterList.toString() inlined parameter values into the SQL text and wrote numeric values without quotes, so a negative number placed right after a '-' in the query template formed a '--' line comment and changed how the rest of the query parsed; the fix writes every value as a quoted literal with a type cast inside parentheses (quoteAndCast).
notes: Fix spans two consecutive commits on master (93b0fcb adds quoteAndCast, 06abfb7 on top of it), first released in REL42.7.2. Backports 42.2.28, 42.3.9, 42.4.4, 42.5.5 and 42.6.1 were not checked. Only reachable with the non-default connection property preferQueryMode=simple.

root_cause: PropertyUtilsBean followed caller-supplied property paths and by default suppressed only the 'class' property, so an enum's 'declaringClass' property still reached a Class object and its ClassLoader; the fix adds SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_DECLARING_CLASS and registers it by default in resetBeanIntrospectors().
notes: The fix commit is on the 2.x line (package beanutils2, fixed in 2.0.0-M2); the 1.x fix (1.11.0, package org.apache.commons.beanutils) was not checked. Correction to the record: the commit adds the SUPPRESS_DECLARING_CLASS constant itself; what existed before was the general SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector class, which callers could configure but which did not cover 'declaringClass' by default.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: The tarfile 'data' and 'tar' extraction filters checked that targets stay inside the destination with os.path.realpath(), which in its default non-strict mode returns a partly resolved path instead of failing when symlink expansion exceeds PATH_MAX, while extraction then used the unresolved path and the OS followed the links outside; the fix uses realpath(strict=ALLOW_MISSING), normalizes link targets and re-applies the filter when extracting links.
notes: One fix (PR #135037, merged into main on 2025-06-03) covers CVE-2024-12718, CVE-2025-4138, CVE-2025-4330 and CVE-2025-4517. Fixed releases per the advisory: 3.9.23, 3.10.18, 3.11.13, 3.12.11, 3.13.4; the backport commits were not checked. The non-strict realpath behavior lives in Lib/posixpath.py (Lib/ntpath.py on Windows); give it to the audit with tarfile.py. Only extraction with the 'data' or 'tar' filter is affected.

root_cause: When two parameters shared one path segment separated by a character other than '.', both got the same default pattern (any character except the delimiter), so both capture groups could consume the separator and a failing match backtracked over every split; the fix makes the later parameter's pattern exclude the preceding text, and 8.0.0 removed the syntax.
notes: Refs use the 6.x fix f1253b4 ('Add backtrack protection to 6.x', fixed in 6.3.0), where parse() sets the default parameter pattern. Other lines: 29b96b4 for 0.1.x (0.1.10, index.js), 925ac8e for 1.x (1.9.0, adds restrictBacktrack in index.js), d31670a for 3.x (3.3.0). 7.x users must move to 8.0.0, which rewrote the API (advisory also lists commit 60f2121e9b66b7b622cc01080df0aabda9eedee6).

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The Node httpAdapter handled 'data:' URLs in a separate branch that decoded the whole payload in memory with fromDataURI(), while maxContentLength and maxBodyLength were only enforced on the HTTP stream branch; the fix estimates the decoded size before decoding and rejects it above maxContentLength.
notes: Refs are the 1.x fix (PR #7011, released in 1.12.0; affected 1.0.0 to 1.11.x), which adds lib/helpers/estimateDataURLDecodedBytes.js. The 0.x line (0.28.0 to 0.30.1, fixed in 0.30.2) was fixed through PR #7034; the advisory also lists commits a1b1d3f073a988601583a604f5f9f5d05a3d0b67 and c30252f685e8f4326722de84923fcbc8cf557f06, which were not read. Node.js only.
